how_daniel_actually_starts.1_ezekiel_closes: the hard close gate passes and the completion receipt is written. The close itself is what 'the book is done' means - not the final check's verdict and not the last apply.
how_daniel_actually_starts.2_orchestrator_stops: OW-9: it does not open Daniel, does not start Phase 0 and does not launch a probe. It saves the resume prompt slot, verifies it mechanically, and PRINTS IT IN FULL in the chat - saving and attaching does not satisfy this, because a file the owner has to open is not a prompt they can paste.
how_daniel_actually_starts.3_owner_clears_and_reprompts: the owner clears the session and pastes that text. That paste is what opens Daniel.
how_daniel_actually_starts.4_phase_0_runs: staging, tooling, byte-proofs and the book strategy - the items listed under phase0_must_produce below.
how_daniel_actually_starts.the_one_mechanism_still_unverified: the resume-prompt generator has never been run against a real close-time state JSON, because that file does not exist until Ezekiel closes. Its source was verified by py_compile and by counting its own clauses, and its EMITTED artifact has not been. That is the single mechanical risk in step 2 and it is stated rather than assumed away.

ISLAND DISCLOSURE SYMMETRY: any row whose span covers the island must say Aramaic somewhere, because the island is a first-order literary fact of that stretch and shipping a row over it silently is a disclosure gap
evidence_2_the_mechanism_was_already_exe.ezekiel_carries_the_same_api_with_two_ar: Ezekiel's member documents its arms 2 and 3 as inert because it has no island. Those are exactly the two arms Daniel activates, so the adaptation path is already named in the code.

THE_GAP_THAT_IS_GENUINELY_NEW.finding: Daniel's island boundary falls MID-VERSE, at 2:4 - the Aramaic runs 2:4b to 7:28. Jeremiah's island is a WHOLE VERSE (10:11), and the disclosure-symmetry arm is verse-granular: it asks whether a row covering the island says 'Aramaic'. It has no notion of a verse that is half Hebrew and half Aramaic.
THE_GAP_THAT_IS_GENUINELY_NEW.why_it_matters: the row containing Dan 2:4 is bilingual WITHIN ONE VERSE. Three things the existing arm cannot express: which half a quotation came from, whether a boundary may fall at the language switch itself, and how a device census reports a verse whose two halves belong to different languages. A formula count that sums across the switch will report false absences in both directions.
THE_GAP_THAT_IS_GENUINELY_NEW.when_to_settle_it: BEFORE mass review, not during. This is the standing method's section 5 and it is the mistake Ezekiel already paid for: 145 units were reviewed on an UNSTATED paragraph-mark convention and the direction had to be settled mid-wave. The sequencing error was the defect, not the units.
THE_GAP_THAT_IS_GENUINELY_NEW.whose_call: the controlling agent's, at Daniel's Phase 0, under OW-6b - not the orchestrator's, and not this file's. It is recorded here so it is a decision rather than a discovery.

fourth_new_thing_found_during_ezekiel.finding: Ezekiel's verse_inventory.json carries a numbering face and declares none. MEASURED: its only top-level keys are book, total_verses and chapters; its chapter 20 is 49 and chapter 21 is 32, which is the WEB face exactly, against MT 44 and 37. A tool that read chapter lengths from it and did verse arithmetic near the zone was therefore wrong and could not know it - that is what happened to the orchestrator's own peer-scoping builder.
fourth_new_thing_found_during_ezekiel.why_it_is_worse_for_daniel: Daniel carries TWO numbering zones, MT 3:31-33 = WEB 4:1-3 and MT 6:1 = WEB 5:31. One undeclared face plus two zones means every adjacency computation near either zone is silently wrong, and the bilingual island boundary at 2:4b sits between them.
fourth_new_thing_found_during_ezekiel.phase0_precondition: Daniel's verse inventory - and every artifact carrying per-chapter counts - MUST declare its face, and every consumer that does verse arithmetic MUST assert the face it expects rather than infer it. Verify this before any tool computes an adjacency, not after.
